exposure: Eligibility for the universal two-child policy
cohort: 2,000 pregnant women in Chengdu, China, who were eligible for the universal two-child policy (case group) compared to 2,000 pregnant women from the same institutions before the policy implementation (comparison group).
finding: Pregnant women eligible for the universal two-child policy were more likely to be older, have a higher household income, work in a non-state-owned enterprise/institution, and have a history of cesarean section, gestational hypertension, gestational diabetes mellitus, and placenta previa.
